title: Intergrown Lenticular Plates and Sandy Matrix Desert Rose
description: One wholly newly authored opaque desert-rose gypsum aggregate at approximately six-centimetre specimen scale. Nine broad biconvex lenticular plates taper to thin gently irregular edges and intergrow in different orientations through one compact sandy mineral matrix. Every entire plate is a closed solid with a verified interior attachment witness to the whole matrix. The matrix has a finite flat underside datum for placement, without a separate museum plinth. All lens profiles, face fields, intergrowth orientations, matrix outline and coordinates are new; no pointed prism, old crystal assembly, recolour or scaled specimen reused. One complete mineral prop, zero scenes, three solid rough sand and ochre PBR roles. Stylized visible morphology only: not measured crystallographic axes, chemical identification, translucency, individual embedded sand grains, a locality-specific specimen, geological process or physical-fracture simulation. No rig, animation or interaction made or verified.
